title: Claude writes your commit messages
blurb: Turns what you actually changed into a clear commit message, so your history is still readable months later.
newcomerProblem: You write "fix" or "update" as the message because thinking of a good one is the last thing between you and being done.
tryThisExplain: Stage some changes with git add, then type this in Claude Code.
explain: Claude reads the changes you have staged and writes the message for you, describing what changed and why rather than repeating the file names. It shows you the message first — nothing is committed until you say so.
honestLimit: It can only describe what it can see in the change. If the reason lives in a ticket or a conversation, you still need to add that yourself.
